name: Wind-Down Routine
description: A simple set of evening steps to ease from the day toward rest. It is a routine you can adapt to your own life. It is not a sleep treatment or medical advice.

steps.text: Pick a time in the evening to stop work and put away any tasks for later.
Dim the lights and tidy one small area of the room.
Write down anything on your mind so it can wait until the morning.
Do a gentle stretch or a few slow breaths, whatever feels pleasant.
Move to your bed or a comfortable chair and let the routine end without any pressure to fall asleep.
If rest is a persistent concern, talk with a clinician.

claims.text: A clear cutoff for work in the evening may make it easier to switch off.
Softer lighting in the evening may feel more relaxing for some people.
Writing down thoughts can be a way to set them aside for later.
Light stretching is commonly described as a pleasant way to release tension.
Letting go of the aim to fall asleep may feel less stressful than trying hard to do so.

safety_notes: Not medical advice and not a sleep treatment for any condition.
Refer persistent sleep trouble to a clinician.
Stop any stretch that causes pain, dizziness or discomfort.
